summary: Round 4, scoped to the delta since a351aa9e. All four round-3 minors are genuinely closed, and two of them I verified by measurement rather than by reading. R3b: with the pointer PUT looped per CommitRequest, CheckpointDiscoveryTest now FAILS (11 tests, 1 failed) where the author reports it previously survived the whole build; looped per POD it also fails, so the strengthened `.as()` label -- 'not per stream, not per pod, not per request' -- is supported in every dimension it names. The full :sequencer suite is green in my tree with the fixture change in place. R3b's helper change is contained: commitOne is private static to CheckpointDiscoveryTest, no other file uses it, and no assertion in that file observes podId or segment keys, so renaming the pods to `pod + request` (and hence 'poda' -> 'poda0' for every one-request caller) changes nothing any test can see; the per-pod discrimination does not depend on that renaming either, since the second trigger already introduces a second pod name. R3a: I grepped the tree independently for the retracted claim. The only remaining occurrences of `list`-and-take-last are the M4 SPEC's AC5 and T1 rows, ADR-0034's Alternatives, the backlog rows and CheckpointDiscoveryTest's own class javadoc -- all describing the REJECTED mechanism -- plus CommitLog/ChainReplayNonDeltaKeyTest/Invariants, which are about chainEnd taking the last DELTA key and are true. There is no fourth site. R3c: the rounds:M4.8c entry is accurate against .harness -- every finding across rounds 1-3 was a test or prose defect, no production behaviour was changed by review, and the two corrected cost arguments it names map to R2a (the per-ancestor clause) and R2c (the ground for keeping the seq-keyed objects, i.e. the second PUT), both corrected in the tree. R3d is correct as far as it goes. Two minors, both prose completeness, both recorded rather than fixed: rule minors-land, and the two-round-cap warning that the next round's surface is the prose a fix adds. Nothing in this delta changes an object-store request rate: the only production edit is a javadoc, and the test edit adds one CommitRequest to one existing commitAll, which strengthens rather than relaxes the pointer's per-trigger bound.

findings.blocks_reason: review.md `minors-land`: on a pass a minor is recorded in the commit body and the commit lands. Recorded rather than fixed because the steer this paragraph gives -- bound the WALK -- is correct and points the right way, and `two-round-cap` warns that redrafting it a fourth time is what buys round 5. This is the third correction of the same paragraph.
findings.title: The new O(epochs walked) paragraph presents the per-ancestor cost as arriving with checkpoint discovery, when the walk already costs one LIST and one stat per ancestor in the landed tree
findings.detail: The added paragraph says 'ONE stat PER ANCESTOR IS CHEAP BUT NOT BOUNDED ... it is O(epochs walked), and an outage that burns a run of epochs makes that a page-count weakening in a new dimension. M4.9 needs a bound on the WALK, not only on the replay.' Every clause is true, but the dimension is not new and the stat is not the whole of it. replayAncestry already calls firstEntry(chainEpoch) once per epoch walked -- one stat plus, when slot 0 exists, one get -- and applyChain issues at least one list per hop; firstInheritableAncestor walks the same way through the same primitive. The M4.9 notes row already measures exactly this on the staged tree: '1 prior term 17/26, 2 terms 32/43, 4 terms 62/77, 8 terms 122/145, 16 terms 242/281. LISTs and stats each grow 3/4/6/10/18 -- one more of each per ancestor -- so bounding GETs alone would leave two request classes still scaling.' So the per-ancestor stat this paragraph names doubles an existing per-ancestor stat and sits beside an existing per-ancestor LIST, and the LIST is the verb the M4 SPEC's AC5 bounds at ZERO. The same 'in a new dimension' phrasing is carried into the backlog-done row.
findings.suggestion: Say that the walk is ALREADY O(epochs) -- firstEntry stats slot 0 once per ancestor and applyChain lists once per hop, measured on M4.9's own row -- so the checkpoint pointer adds a constant factor to an unbounded walk rather than introducing one, and AC5's zero-list clause cannot be met without changing that walk. Or drop the forward-looking clause entirely and leave the steer, which is the remedy M4.8b1's row records for a paragraph redrafted three times.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever builds M4.9 reads this javadoc, treats the per-ancestor stat as the new hazard, bounds the number of pointer stats, and lands 'bounded recovery' with the per-ancestor LIST from applyChain and the per-ancestor stat from firstEntry still in place -- AC5 requires zero lists in recovery, and a workload with one ancestor passes a request-count assertion written against it while a cluster with a run of burned epochs pays one list plus two stats per epoch on every takeover. The corrective fact exists only in backlog-notes.md, which a session is told to read one row of, and the row it would read is M4.9's -- so this is recoverable, which is why it is minor rather than major.

findings.blocks_reason: review.md `minors-land`. The entry is accurate as written; this is an omission, and baselines/review.txt entries are harvested at the milestone boundary under `minors-at-milestone`.
findings.title: The rewritten rounds:M4.8c entry records round 2's transferable lesson and not round 3's, though round 3 exists because the round-2 lesson was not applied to a claim
findings.detail: The entry keeps 'WHEN A MUTANT IS FOUND, FIND EVERY SITE OF ITS SHAPE, not the one reported' from round 2, and adds an accurate retraction of the flattering 'survived every round untouched'. What it does not carry is what round 3 actually found: the same lesson applies to a RETRACTED CLAIM, and it was not applied -- the list-and-take-last sentence was corrected in LogKeys and in ADR-0034 and left standing at a third site one commit later, and an `.as()` label claimed a discrimination the fixture could not make. The backlog-done row records both; baselines/review.txt does not. That file is what a session reads when it argues past the cap, and its peer entries (rounds:M4.8b1, rounds:M4.7, rounds:M0.53) all carry the lesson rather than only the outcome.
findings.suggestion: Add one clause: that round 3 found the round-2 lesson stated in this very entry and not applied one commit later, to a claim rather than to a mutant -- and that the remedy is a grep for every site of a retracted sentence, not a fix at the site a reviewer names. Or leave it, since backlog-done.md carries it; recording in the commit body is enough.
findings.failure_scenario: A later session past the round cap reads this entry for precedent, takes 'find every site of a mutant's shape' as the whole lesson, retracts a claim at the one site a reviewer names, and buys the round M4.8c bought -- the entry that would have prevented it is the one describing the task where it happened.
